explanations.explanation: Isaiah 30:18 says, “Therefore the LORD longs to be gracious to you…” Longs, friend. That's a long way from putting up with them. After all that running and refusing, I think that word is a soft place to land.

Egypt is where the people ran for help (Isaiah 30:2), not what the LORD longs to do. The verse says He “…longs to be gracious to you…” It also says He “…rises to show you compassion…” Handing them over isn't in the verse.

The people did say they would flee on horses (Isaiah 30:16). But the LORD's answer in this verse is that He “…longs to be gracious to you…” Then He “…rises to show you compassion…” That's not a God walking off, friend.

The verse ends, “Blessed are all who wait for Him.” Waiting is hard work, friend. I've stared at a timer with nine minutes left like it was telling me fibs. Still, the blessing goes to the ones who wait.
Speed doesn't get the blessing here. Isaiah 30:18 says, “Blessed are all who wait for Him.” Nothing about who gets there first. The blessing goes to the waiters, not the racers.

explanations.answer: All who make their own plans
explanations.explanation: Plans are fine, friend, I make them every batch. But this verse hands the blessing to a different group. It says, “Blessed are all who wait for Him.” Waiting on Him is what the prophet calls blessed.

Not quite, friend. Isaiah 30:19 says, “He will surely be gracious when you cry for help; when He hears, He will answer you.” So when He hears, He answers. The silence in this question isn't in the verse.

Right, friend, it's false. Isaiah 30:19 says, “He will surely be gracious when you cry for help; when He hears, He will answer you.” He hears and He answers. And the verse also says the people will weep no more.

explanations.answer: He will no longer hide Himself
explanations.explanation: Yes, friend. Isaiah 30:20 says, “…your Teacher will no longer hide Himself…” And the people will see Him with their own eyes. The bread of adversity and the water of affliction come, but the Teacher is seen right there in it.

explanations.answer: He will leave them on their own
explanations.explanation: The verse goes the other direction, friend. Hard days come, the bread of adversity and the water of affliction. But Isaiah 30:20 says, “…your Teacher will no longer hide Himself…” A Teacher in plain sight isn't leaving anybody on their own.

explanations.answer: He will only speak in dreams
explanations.explanation: Dreams aren't mentioned in this verse at all. What it says is that their Teacher “…will no longer hide Himself…” And they will see Him with their own eyes. That's about as far from dreams-only as you can get.

Yes, friend, behind. Isaiah 30:21 says, “…your ears will hear this command behind you…” Turn right, turn left, the voice is still back there. Some of us will take any help we can get from behind, especially when we're SURE we know where we're going.
The verse doesn't send the voice up high. Isaiah 30:21 says, “…your ears will hear this command behind you…” It's close enough to hear, whichever way they turn. Behind is the answer.
No building in this verse, friend. It talks about turning right or left, and the command comes “behind you.” Wherever they turn, the voice is behind them.
Yes, friend. Isaiah 30:22 says, “You will throw them away…” All that silver-plating and gold-plating, and the people tell those idols, “Be gone!” Shiny doesn't mean it stays on the shelf.
Nobody's cashing anything in here, friend. The verse says they will desecrate the idols and “…throw them away…” No melting and no coins. They say to them, “Be gone!”
There's no 'later' in this verse, friend. Isaiah 30:22 says, “You will throw them away…” They don't hold anything back for a rainy day. They say, “Be gone!”
Rain, friend. Isaiah 30:23 says, “Then He will send rain for the seed that you have sown in the ground…” A seed with no rain is just a very patient pebble. This time the rain comes to it.

Locusts would be a rough day for any seed, but they aren't in this verse. Isaiah 30:23 says, “Then He will send rain for the seed that you have sown in the ground…” The seed gets rain, and the verse goes on to rich and plentiful food.

Frost isn't anywhere in this verse, friend. Isaiah 30:23 says, “Then He will send rain for the seed that you have sown in the ground…” The seed gets rain, and the food that comes will be rich and plentiful.
True, friend. Isaiah 30:23 says the food that comes from the land “…will be rich and plentiful.” I bake by the batch, and even I'd call that a lot. The cattle graze in open pastures that same day.

It's true, friend. Isaiah 30:23 says the food that comes from the land “…will be rich and plentiful.” The rain comes first and then the food follows. And that day the cattle graze in open pastures too.

explanations.answer: Every high mountain and raised hill
explanations.explanation: Yes, friend. Isaiah 30:25 says, “And from every high mountain and every raised hill, streams of water will flow…” Water usually collects down low. Here it's flowing from the high places, every one of them.
The verse doesn't point to the temple. Isaiah 30:25 says the streams flow “…from every high mountain and every raised hill…” The water starts up in the high places.
No rock in this verse, friend. The streams of water come “…from every high mountain and every raised hill…” (Isaiah 30:25). The high places are where the water flows from.

Heals, friend. Isaiah 30:26 says it's “…the day that the LORD binds up the brokenness of His people and heals the wounds He has inflicted.” Binds up and heals, both on that day. And the moon shines like the sun.

That's a nice word, but it isn't the one in the verse. Isaiah 30:26 says the LORD “…binds up the brokenness of His people and heals the wounds He has inflicted.” The word is heals. The brokenness gets bound up.

Close in sound, friend, but the verse says something else. Isaiah 30:26 says the LORD “…binds up the brokenness of His people and heals the wounds He has inflicted.” He heals, and that's the day the moon shines like the sun.

Not quite, friend. Isaiah 30:28 says He comes “…to sift the nations in a sieve of destruction…” It's the nations being sifted. His people don't get named as the ones in that sieve, and the next verse turns to them singing.
Right, friend, it's false. Isaiah 30:28 says He comes “…to sift the nations in a sieve of destruction…” The sieve is for the nations. Then the prophet turns back to His people, and they sing.

explanations.answer: Sing as on a holy festival night
explanations.explanation: Yes, friend. Isaiah 30:29 says, “You will sing as on the night of a holy festival…” Their heart rejoices like one who walks to the music of a flute, going up to the mountain of the LORD. After all that fire and smoke in the verses before, singing is the sound that follows for His people.

No hiding in this verse, friend. Isaiah 30:29 says, “You will sing as on the night of a holy festival…” Their heart rejoices like one who walks to the music of a flute, going up to the mountain of the LORD.

Egypt isn't in this verse, friend. Isaiah 30:29 says, “You will sing as on the night of a holy festival…” The going up to “…the mountain of the LORD, to the Rock of Israel.” is part of a picture of rejoicing. No Egypt anywhere in sight.

Yes, friend. Isaiah 30:30 says His arm is revealed “…striking in angry wrath with a flame of consuming fire, and with cloudburst, storm, and hailstones.” That's a heavy picture, so I'll just let the verse say it. Fire and hailstones are both right there in it.

Neither one shows up in this verse, friend. Isaiah 30:30 lists “…a flame of consuming fire, and with cloudburst, storm, and hailstones.” A cloudburst is about as far from a drought as weather gets. Fire and hailstones are the pair.
That's not on this verse's list, friend. Isaiah 30:30 says “…a flame of consuming fire, and with cloudburst, storm, and hailstones.” So it's fire and hailstones that come with His voice and His arm.
Yes, friend. Isaiah 30:31 says, “For Assyria will be shattered at the voice of the LORD…” Not a whisper of negotiation. It's shattered at His voice, and He strikes them with His scepter.

explanations.answer: It will be humbled and spared
explanations.explanation: Spared isn't in this verse, friend. Isaiah 30:31 says, “For Assyria will be shattered at the voice of the LORD…” and that He will strike them with His scepter. Shattered is the word the prophet uses.

explanations.answer: It will make peace with Judah
explanations.explanation: No peace talks in this verse, friend. The prophet says, “For Assyria will be shattered at the voice of the LORD…” and that He will strike them with His scepter. A treaty doesn't show up anywhere in it.

True, friend. Isaiah 30:32 says that with every stroke of the rod, “…the tambourines and lyres will sound…” So there's music playing along with every stroke. Tambourines and lyres together, that's a whole band.
It's true, friend. Isaiah 30:32 says that with every stroke of the rod of punishment, “…the tambourines and lyres will sound…” Every stroke has its own sound of tambourines and lyres.

Yes, friend, breath. Isaiah 30:33 says, “The breath of the LORD, like a torrent of burning sulfur, sets it ablaze.” This is a heavy part of the passage, so I'll leave it right there. Earlier the prophet said His breath is like a rushing torrent (Isaiah 30:28).
No angel in this verse, friend. Isaiah 30:33 says, “The breath of the LORD, like a torrent of burning sulfur, sets it ablaze.” This is a heavy verse, so I'll keep it simple. The word is breath.

An altar isn't mentioned in this verse, friend. What's there is a funeral pyre, deep and wide, with plenty of fire and wood. It's a heavy verse. Isaiah 30:33 says “The breath of the LORD, like a torrent of burning sulfur, sets it ablaze.”
